section.title: Clone Repository
section.p: Use: Creates a local copy of a remote Git repository in a new folder. A clone includes the repository data and enough history to let you work locally, commit changes, and synchronize with the remote repository later.

Details: You provide the remote repository URL, the destination path, and optionally a branch to checkout. If you do not choose a branch, Git uses the default branch configured by the remote repository. Specify a branch only when you do not want to clone the repository default branch. After the clone operation finishes, the new repository becomes the current working copy in the Git Client.
When to Use: Use this action when the repository does not exist yet on your computer or when you need a fresh local copy of a remote repository.

ul.li: Ellipsis menu in the Git Staging view toolbar.

section.title: Open Repository or Select Working Copy
section.p: Use: Selects an existing local Git repository as the current working copy. A working copy is the local folder where Git stores the files you edit and tracks their changes against the repository history.

Details: The selected folder must already be a Git repository. After you select it, the Git Client reads its current branch, staged and unstaged changes, remote tracking state, and history. Most actions in the Git menu and the Git Staging view then apply to this repository.

When to Use: Use this action when the repository already exists on your computer and you want to make it the active repository in the Git Client. When a working copy is opened, the Git Client can also detect outdated local branches in the background.

ul.li: Open repository... in the Git menu.
Browse button next to the Working copy combo box in the Git Staging view.

section.title: Create Repository in Project
section.p: Use: Initializes a Git repository in the current project folder. This creates the Git repository data needed for Git to start tracking changes in that folder.

Details: The action applies to the project folder loaded in the Project view. The new repository starts as a local repository. It does not automatically have a remote repository, so push and pull operations require a remote repository URL when you first synchronize changes.

When to Use: Use this action when you have local project files that are not yet under Git control and you want to start tracking their changes. The action is enabled only when the project folder is not already part of a Git repository.

ul.li: Ellipsis menu in the Git Staging view toolbar.

section.title: Create Repository Here
section.p: Use: Initializes a Git repository in a selected folder from the Project view. This lets you start tracking a folder even when it is not the root folder of the current project.

Details: The action creates a local repository in the selected project folder. Git then treats that folder as a working copy and can detect modified, added, and deleted files under it. The repository is local until you connect it to a remote repository and push changes.
When to Use: Use this action when only one folder in the project should become a Git repository. The action is available when the selected folder is not already part of a local Git repository.
Accessible From: Git submenu in the Project view contextual menu.

section.title: Show Working Copy in Finder
section.p: Use: Opens the current working copy folder in Finder so you can inspect the files in the operating system file browser.

Details: This action does not change the repository. It opens the folder that is currently selected as the Git Client working copy. Use it when you need to copy files, inspect generated output, or use operating system file actions outside .

ul.li: Git menu: GitShow working copy inFinder.
Ellipsis menu in the Git Staging view toolbar.

section.title: Show Working Copy in Terminal
section.p: Use: Opens a terminal window in the current working copy folder so you can run Git or operating system commands from that repository location.

Details: This action does not run a Git command and does not change the repository. It only opens the terminal in the working copy folder, which is useful when you need a command that is not exposed in the Git Client or when you need to inspect repository state with Git command-line tools.

ul.li: Git menu: GitShow working copy inTerminal.
Ellipsis menu in the Git Staging view toolbar.
